pages.title: About the studio
pages.content:
ABOUT

Founded in 2011 by Mira Halvorsen, Otonoha Acoustics is an independent architectural acoustic consultancy of seven people based in Calder Wharf. We measure offices, classrooms, lecture rooms, and small halls before interior finishes are specified.

Why the Studio Was Founded

Otonoha means leaves of sound in Japanese. In 2011, Mira Halvorsen established the consultancy around a single observation: interior finishes are frequently specified from swatch books without measuring the physical room first. Once acoustic plaster, mineral tile, or perforated timber are installed, correcting acoustic imbalance becomes costly and disruptive. We work with architects, building owners, and project teams across Calder Wharf and beyond to document the acoustic behaviour of raw spaces. Each room is read leaf by leaf, assessing reverberation, background noise, partition sound insulation, and speech clarity before final surface contracts are committed.

How a Survey Day Runs

Every survey follows five structured stages during a single site day. At 08:30, our team walks the empty room with project drawings open, inspecting spatial volume, junction details, and structural boundaries. Testing commences at 09:30, measuring reverberation decay across octave bands and logging baseline background noise from street traffic and mechanical plant. At 12:00, we conduct speech transmission index measurements and sound insulation testing across critical partitions. By 15:00, we sit down with you on site to review initial raw findings and immediate physical impressions. Exactly ten working days later, we deliver the comprehensive written acoustic report alongside a thirty-minute consultation call.

The Consultancy Team

Our practice operates as a close-knit group of seven specialists. Mira Halvorsen serves as founder and principal consultant, leading room acoustics and hall surveys. Tomas Achterberg is senior consultant specialising in sound insulation and floor build-ups. Leila Farouk leads classroom surveys and speech intelligibility assessments. Priya Venkataraman consults on open-plan office layouts and speech privacy. Daniel Osei serves as field engineer, managing instrument calibration, microphone arrays, and dodecahedron loudspeaker placement. Sofia Rinaldi acts as report editor, drafting architectural drawings, material schedules, and absorption maps. Jun-ho Park coordinates bookings, travel logistics, and client communications from our Calder Wharf studio.

Studio Facts and Working Hours

Otonoha Acoustics operates from Studio 4, 18 Ferrow Lane, Calder Wharf. Founded in 2011, our independent team of seven maintains office and telephone enquiry hours Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 17:30. On-site survey visits take place Monday to Saturday, beginning at 08:30 for daytime work, or during dedicated evening sessions from 18:00 to 22:00 for facilities occupied throughout regular business hours. We remain closed on Sundays and public holidays. Direct telephone enquiries reach +00 31 555 0186, and written requests can be sent to survey@otonoha-acoustics.example. Travel within 80 kilometres of Calder Wharf is included in standard fees.

pages.title: Rooms we survey
pages.content:
ROOMS

Auditorium

Tiered, 420 seats · RT target 1.0–1.2 s

Classroom

30 desks · RT target 0.6–0.8 s

Small hall

200 seats · RT target 1.4–1.8 s

Open office

90 desks · speech privacy by zone

We measure four distinct room types using consistent physical methodology before finish schedules are locked. Every survey assesses raw architectural boundaries when spaces are unoccupied.

Classrooms and Small Meeting Rooms

Classrooms and seminar rooms up to 300 m³ suffer primarily from flutter echoes, excessive reverberation, and speech masking caused by reflective hard walls and unbaffled ceilings. During a small-room survey, we measure reverberation decay across standard octave bands and calculate speech transmission index values at listening positions. The recognized target range for classroom reverberation time is 0.6 to 0.8 seconds. Measurements reveal whether conversational clarity requires ceiling absorption or wall panelling. This evaluation falls under our small-room survey tier at €680. If additional classrooms in the same building are surveyed during the same visit, each is charged at the supplementary rate of €420.

Lecture Rooms and Large Teaching Spaces

Tiered lecture halls and large instruction spaces between 300 and 2,000 m³ present complex acoustic challenges. Late sound reflections from distant rear walls and concave ceiling geometries frequently muddle syllables for listeners seated beyond the sixth row. We record decay curves, early-to-late sound energy ratios, and ambient ventilation plant noise. The acoustic target range for spoken lecture presentation is 0.7 to 0.9 seconds. Our survey determines the precise distribution of absorptive rear finishes and diffusive ceiling treatments needed before construction contracts close. This service is priced under our room survey category at €1,180, with supplementary rooms on the same visit billed at €420.

The room is measured empty, so the numbers describe the room and not the people in it.

Small hall, after hours

Open-Plan Office Floors

Commercial office floors ranging between 300 and 2,000 m² often experience sound propagation issues where conversational speech carries unimpeded across desk clusters, destroying focus. In these environments, we quantify background noise curves from central air handlers, measure spatial sound decay rates, and evaluate speech privacy radii between team work zones. The acoustic objective is not silence, but containing voice intelligibility to immediate clusters through balanced ambient noise and targeted absorption. An open-office floor evaluation falls under our room survey tier at €1,180. The resulting report outlines specific placement for acoustic ceiling rafts, wall absorbers, and partition screens.

Auditoriums and Small Music Halls

Performance venues, auditoriums, and recital halls between 2,000 and 8,000 m³ (seating up to 600 people) require careful energy balance between clarity and warmth. Excessive high-frequency absorption leaves musical performance dry and lifeless, while insufficient low-frequency control muddies fast acoustic passages. For chamber music performance, we target a balanced reverberation time of 1.4 to 1.8 seconds. We place calibrated omnidirectional sound sources on stage and map energy distribution throughout stalls and balconies. This comprehensive acoustic assessment is priced under our hall survey tier at €2,400. If partition sound transmission to backstage rooms requires testing, partition tests are €360 each.

Small halls for music

A small hall for chamber music sits between these two cases. It is measured the same way, empty and with the drawings open, and its target is set against the music it will host. Ask for the hall survey fee on the fees page.

Book a room survey →

pages.title: The report
pages.content:
REPORT

Delivered in ten working days following our on-site survey, the Otonoha report translates calibrated measurements into clear architectural specifications. Every report is divided into four standard parts.

Four parts

Ten working days

Every report gives clear data and practical guidance to adjust finishes before procurement.

Part 01

Reverberation curves by octave band

Part 02

Background noise and plant

Part 03

Insulation between rooms

Part 04

Finish-schedule proposals

Part 1: Reverberation Curves by Octave Band

The opening section of the report documents measured reverberation decay times from 63 Hz to 8,000 Hz across multiple microphone receiver positions. We present individual decay curves alongside mean values and contrast them against recommended international acoustic standards for your room type. Whether evaluating a classroom requiring 0.6 to 0.8 seconds or a recital space targeted at 1.4 to 1.8 seconds, raw data is plotted clearly. Graphic visualisations show early decay time, mid-frequency averages, and bass ratios, highlighting precisely which frequency bands require acoustic attenuation or reflection preservation before interior wall finishes are purchased.

Part 2: Background Noise and Mechanical Plant

Part two presents continuous spectrum measurements of ambient background noise recorded during daytime and evening operation. We measure noise criteria curves, sound pressure levels in dBA, and individual octave bands to identify intrusive noise generated by external road traffic, lifts, and building mechanical services. If ventilation fan hum or chiller vibrations mask unamplified speech in a lecture hall or exceed privacy criteria in an open office, the report isolates the offending frequencies. These baseline measurements give building services engineers and architects unambiguous target levels for attenuators, duct linings, and acoustic casing specifications.

Part 3: Sound Insulation Between Adjacent Rooms

Where sound insulation testing was commissioned at €360 per partition, part three details sound transmission losses across dividing walls and floor slabs. Using calibrated loudspeaker sources and receiving microphones, we record standardized level differences and weighted sound reduction indices. Flanking transmission pathways through continuous ceiling plenums, perimeter window mullions, and floor voids are identified in architectural section drawings. The report explains whether wall density, cavity insulation, or junction decoupling is required to achieve desired privacy between confidential meeting suites, classrooms, or performance auditoriums and adjacent circulation corridors.

Part 4: Finish-Schedule Proposals and Boundaries

The final section provides actionable material proposals specifying necessary absorption coefficients, required surface areas, and recommended room locations such as rear walls, ceiling soffits, or perimeter bulkheads. We outline generic material types, including slatted timber, perforated board, or fabric-wrapped mineral panels, without commercial bias. Otonoha Acoustics sells no proprietary acoustic panels and receives no commercial commissions. Our practice provides acoustic measurement and finish guidance without structural engineering certifications or product sales. Our recommendations remain independent architectural advice designed to guide your project team before contracts are awarded. Every survey includes a thirty-minute consultation call to review these finish proposals.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
FEES

We maintain six transparent acoustic survey fees, fixed in euros before we travel. Every booking includes on-site measurement, a written report delivered in ten working days, and a thirty-minute review call.

Standard Survey Fee Schedule

Inclusions, Travel Rates, and Payment Terms

Each survey fee covers physical site inspection, equipment calibration, the complete written report delivered in ten working days, and a thirty-minute follow-up phone call with your consultant. Travel to project sites within 80 kilometres of our Calder Wharf studio is included without extra charge. For locations beyond 80 kilometres, travel is billed at €0.60 per return kilometre. All quoted prices exclude VAT. Invoices are issued upon report delivery, with standard payment terms of 30 days. Cancellations made up to five working days prior to the agreed visit date incur no fee; cancellations made after that deadline are charged at 30 percent of the quoted survey price.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content:
QUESTIONS

Clear answers to common questions regarding survey requirements, building access, report delivery, and consultancy terms. If your question is not listed, contact our studio team directly.

01

Does the room need to be empty?

Yes. The room must be completely unoccupied and quiet for three to four hours during testing. Accurate measurement of reverberation decay and ambient noise requires zero human activity in the testing zone. Work by cleaning staff, building trades, or desk occupants must be paused while sound level meters and calibrated loudspeakers are operating. This quiet window allows us to capture true architectural boundary reflections without intrusive noise artifacts contaminating the acoustic data.

02

Do you offer evening sessions?

Yes. For spaces that remain in active use throughout normal business hours, we provide evening survey sessions between 18:00 and 22:00, Monday through Saturday. This accommodates operational schools, university lecture halls, and busy commercial offices where daytime quiet cannot be scheduled. Evening visits follow the same rigorous testing methodology as our daytime surveys and are charged at our standard published fees without evening surcharges.

03

Can you measure a room under construction?

Yes, provided the building envelope is weather-tight with permanent exterior glazing, exterior doors, and exterior wall framing fully sealed. Testing an unglazed or open shell produces invalid acoustic results because sound escapes rather than reflecting off physical boundaries. However, surveying a room before interior finish schedules, suspended ceilings, and final wall linings are fixed is ideal, as it allows acoustic corrections to be incorporated into early architectural finishes.

04

How long does it take to receive the report?

We deliver the complete written report exactly ten working days after our site survey visit. During these ten working days, our team processes raw impulse responses, plots octave-band decay curves, evaluates noise spectra, and compiles specific material proposals. Along with the digital report, every booking includes a thirty-minute consultation call with your surveyor to answer questions, discuss findings, and guide contractor specifications.

05

Do you sell acoustic panels or materials?

No. Otonoha Acoustics is an entirely independent consultancy. We do not manufacture, sell, distribute, or install acoustic panels, baffles, or insulation products. We maintain no commercial partnerships or affiliate relationships with material manufacturers. Our reports specify required surface absorption coefficients, surface areas, and recommended placement locations using generic material descriptions, allowing you to source finishes from any manufacturer or supplier without conflict of interest.

06

How do you calculate travel fees beyond 80 km?

Survey visits to buildings located within 80 kilometres of our Calder Wharf studio include travel at no additional charge. For site locations exceeding 80 kilometres, travel is billed at a transparent rate of €0.60 per return kilometre from our studio address. Return mileage is calculated in advance and itemized clearly on your formal written fee proposal, ensuring total project expenditure is fixed and agreed before our team departs.

07

What is your cancellation policy?

You may cancel or reschedule an agreed survey visit without financial penalty up to five working days before the scheduled on-site measurement date. If a cancellation occurs fewer than five working days prior to the visit, a fee equal to 30 percent of the agreed survey cost is charged to offset reserved engineering time and equipment preparation. All cancellation requests should be submitted in writing via email.

08

Who owns the survey report and data?

You own the final report and measurement data upon settlement of the invoice. You are free to distribute the documentation to your architects, structural engineers, mechanical contractors, and interior designers as needed for project delivery. Otonoha Acoustics retains copyright over internal calculation methodologies, proprietary drawing templates, and measurement formats, but the specific acoustic figures, decay curves, and site recommendations remain fully licensed to your organisation.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
This privacy policy outlines how Otonoha Acoustics collects, stores, and handles client contact details, site documentation, and technical survey records.

Data Collection and Project Documentation

Otonoha Acoustics collects personal and business information strictly necessary to prepare fee quotations, conduct acoustic surveys, and issue technical reports. Information collected includes client names, organisational affiliations, billing addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses. We also receive architectural drawings, CAD files, photographs, and building access schedules submitted during booking. This documentation is stored on secure internal servers and used solely by our seven studio staff members to carry out commissioned acoustic assessments and administrative tasks.

Data Retention, Third Parties, and Client Rights

We do not sell, rent, or share personal contact data or architectural drawings with third-party advertisers or external contractors. Measurement data and written reports are archived securely for a minimum of ten years to assist clients with future building refurbishments or compliance verification. You have the right to request access to the personal data we hold, request corrections to contact details, or request deletion of non-essential records by writing to survey@otonoha-acoustics.example.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
These terms govern acoustic consultancy services, site survey visits, report delivery, and fee structures provided by Otonoha Acoustics.

Engagement, Survey Conditions, and Delivery

Services are engaged once a formal written quotation is confirmed in writing by the client. The client is responsible for providing clear, uninterrupted access to the building and ensuring quiet conditions for three to four hours during testing. Survey visits take place Monday to Saturday starting from 08:30 or during evening sessions from 18:00 to 22:00. Otonoha Acoustics delivers the written acoustic report within ten working days following the survey visit, including one thirty-minute review phone call.

Fees, Travel, Payment, and Cancellation Terms

All fees are quoted in EUR and exclude VAT. Standard rates are €680 for small rooms up to 300 m³, €1,180 for rooms between 300 and 2,000 m³, €2,400 for halls between 2,000 and 8,000 m³, €420 for additional rooms, €360 per partition insulation test, and €290 for a two-hour review meeting. Travel within 80 kilometres of Calder Wharf is included; travel beyond is billed at €0.60 per return kilometre. Invoices are payable within 30 days of report delivery. Cancellations made up to five working days before the visit incur no charge; cancellations within five working days incur a 30 percent fee.

Scope of Consultancy and Liability Limits

Otonoha Acoustics provides independent acoustic measurement and material recommendations based on physical conditions observed at the time of testing. Our consultancy does not provide structural engineering calculations, building regulation sign-offs, or commercial performance certifications. We sell no acoustic products and accept no responsibility for contractor installation errors or deviation from report specifications. Total liability arising out of any survey or report is strictly limited to the total consultancy fee paid by the client for that specific engagement.

posts.title: A 180-seat lecture room that echoed
posts.excerpt: An acoustic survey of a 1,450 m³ tiered lecture room where excessive mid-frequency reverberation impaired spoken instruction before interior finishes were finalized.
posts.content:
Room type

Tiered lecture room

Volume

1,450 m³

Measured

RT 1.9 s (mid-frequency)

Target

0.7–0.9 s for speech

Consultant

Leila Farouk

Year

2026

In early 2026, Otonoha Acoustics was invited to survey a newly enclosed 180-seat tiered lecture hall measuring approximately 1,450 m³. The structural shell was fully weather-tight, featuring fair-faced painted concrete flank walls, raked concrete floor risers, and an exposed structural ceiling slab. Although the room was intended for university lectures and spoken presentations, initial acoustic impressions indicated substantial flutter echo and ringing resonance across the seating rake, making normal conversation difficult to understand past the third row of seats.

Consultant Leila Farouk conducted the on-site survey starting at 08:30 on a scheduled weekday visit. Using calibrated omnidirectional dodecahedron loudspeakers and precision sound level microphones placed across eight discrete receiver positions, our team recorded impulse responses, speech transmission index values, and baseline background noise. The measured mid-frequency reverberation time averaged 1.9 seconds, with noticeable energy lingering around 500 Hz and 1,000 Hz. For an academic lecture space of 1,450 m³ reliant on unamplified or lightly amplified speech, the recognized target range is 0.7 to 0.9 seconds. The bare room exceeded this benchmark by more than a full second.

Analysis of the raw decay curves revealed that sound energy was reflecting repeatedly between the unyielding parallel side walls and bouncing back into the rear seating rows from the high rear wall. In addition, the hard concrete soffit reflected vocal energy downwards with delayed arrival times, smearing spoken consonant clarity. Background ambient noise from the building air supply measured within normal limits, confirming that reverberation was the dominant source of acoustic degradation. Because the project team had engaged our studio before finishes were specified, the room's interior surface contracts remained open, presenting an ideal window for targeted architectural acoustic interventions without the cost of demolition or retrofit modifications.

The final acoustic report, delivered within our standard ten working days, proposed a coordinated distribution of sound absorption rather than uniform wall cladding. Specifically, the report proposed installing high-performance absorptive fabric-wrapped panels across the upper half of the rear wall to eliminate delayed slap-back reflections to the front lectern. For the ceiling, the report recommended suspended horizontal acoustic baffles arranged above the seating rake, leaving the central ceiling area reflective to preserve natural acoustic projection from the lecturer towards the rear tiers.

Furthermore, the report proposed selective treatment on the side walls, incorporating slatted timber panels backed with mineral insulation along the rear third of each flank. This approach was designed to control lateral flutter echoes while maintaining visual warmth in keeping with the architect's aesthetic intent. Consistent with our independent consultancy practice, Otonoha Acoustics recommended generic material specifications without endorsing proprietary manufacturer products. A follow-up thirty-minute consultation call with the architectural design team reviewed the calculated absorption areas, ensuring that proposed finish materials matched the project's mechanical ventilation paths and lighting layouts prior to contractor tender.

posts.title: Ninety desks, one quiet corner
posts.excerpt: An open-office floor of 1,100 m² with 90 desks: background noise and speech privacy measured zone by zone.
posts.content:
An open-office floor of 1,100 m² with 90 desks. We measured background noise and speech privacy between the team zones in the empty floor, early in the morning.

The report proposed ceiling rafts above the busiest zones and two screens between neighbouring teams, with the measuring points marked on the plan so the fit-out team could see why each item was there. — Priya Venkataraman

posts.title: A small hall for chamber music
posts.excerpt: A 240-seat recital hall of 2,900 m³ measured RT 1.4 s; chamber music asks for 1.6–1.8 s.
posts.content:
A 240-seat recital hall of 2,900 m³. The measured reverberation time was 1.4 s; for chamber music the target was 1.6–1.8 s, so this hall needed less absorption, not more.

The report proposed removing the absorptive panels on the side walls. It stated the measured values and the reasoning, and left the decision with the architect. — Mira Halvorsen
